key_corrections: First-pass said 'No embedded wallet evidence found' — this needs correction. The JS bundle contains 'dynamicEnvironmentId' (Dynamic.xyz wallet connection/embedded wallet SDK) and 'dynamicauth'. Dynamic.xyz supports email, social login, and embedded wallets — similar to Privy but a competing product. However, current docs still describe wallet-first onboarding only.
Extended now has 121 markets on mainnet (was implied to be much smaller in first-pass). Testnet has 31 markets.
Rhino.fi integration confirmed in JS config (rhinoApiKey, rhinoBaseUrl: https://api.rhino.fi) — this powers the Arbitrum cross-chain deposit path documented in the deposit docs.
USDC is the only collateral (not USDT), and Arbitrum deposits/withdrawals are supported for amounts under $100,000.
Python SDK has a 'drop-api-keys' branch, suggesting potential future auth model change.
The build ID (app-exchange-v0-64-18) confirms this is actively maintained and versioned.

TESTNET_CONFIG and MAINNET_CONFIG included

updated_assessment.web2_friendliness: Low-medium, but higher than first-pass described. Dynamic.xyz integration exists in the JS bundle (supporting email/social/embedded wallets), though not yet surfaced in docs or visibly in the UI.
updated_assessment.api_order_usability_from_cold_wallet: High on testnet — first-pass already proved full end-to-end flow (onboard → API key → signed IOC order). Mainnet requires real USDC deposit first.
key_friction_points: Stark key material derivation is heavier than standard EVM signing
Need both API key AND Stark signature for write operations
Key pair stored in browser only (not server-side) — need SDK for programmatic access
Mainnet requires USDC deposit before trading
API management page (UI) needed to get API key details
updated_assessment.what_changed_vs_first_pass: Dynamic.xyz wallet SDK is present (first-pass said no embedded wallet). Market count grew to 121 mainnet. Rhino.fi cross-chain bridging confirmed. 'drop-api-keys' SDK branch hints at potential future auth simplification. Docs now explicitly mention Arbitrum support. Core auth model and testnet onboarding flow unchanged.
updated_assessment.comparison_to_other_platforms: Extended remains the most API-complete platform in the sample for serious integrators — it's the only one where first-pass successfully completed a full write-path probe (onboard → key → signed order). The auth stack is heavy (EVM + Stark + API key), but it's well-documented and fully scriptable.
